name: memory has a Big-O too
hook: Time isn't the only cost. Memory has a Big-O too, and some of it you never typed.
hook_slide: Time isn't the only cost. *Memory has a Big-O too.*
hook_sub: And some of that memory you never typed.
caption: Space complexity is the same O machinery, applied to memory. One distinction does most of the work: total space counts the input, auxiliary space is only the extra you allocate. Auxiliary is what people mean by default.
Finding a max keeps one variable: O(1). Returning a sorted copy of {n} numbers allocates {copy_cells} more slots: O(n).
Then the memory you don't see. Every active call holds a stack frame, so adding 1 to {n} recursively stacks {frames_rec} frames; the loop uses {frames_iter}. Same time complexity, different space.
And at {big} the recursive version isn't slow. It's a stack overflow.
Do you state space when you state time? 👇
cta: See the stack frames drawn, call by call.

p: Total space counts everything, including the input.
*Auxiliary* space is only the extra you allocate. It is what people mean by default, since the input's size isn't something you chose.

slides.h: One variable, or a full copy
p: `max_of` is O(1) auxiliary. `sorted_copy` is O(n): on {n} numbers, {copy_cells} extra slots.

slides.h: Every call holds a stack frame
p: Recursion costs memory proportional to its depth, even if no frame allocates anything.

slides.h: At {big} it is not slow. It is an error.
p: Python's recursion limit and JavaScript engines' stack sizes both turn `sum_to` on {big} into a stack overflow.
From here on, stack depth is always part of the space answer.
